question: Nearly half of holiday decorators admit to daisy-chaining power strips or extension cords -- why does it matter?
verdictConfirmed: ULSE's 2026 survey: 46% admit daisy-chaining power strips or extension cords. UL lists power strips (relocatable power taps) to plug directly into a wall receptacle, not into another strip or an extension cord; chaining adds outlets, not capacity, because every downstream plug draws through the first cord and one branch circuit.

facts.claim: 46% of holiday decorators admit to daisy-chaining power strips or extension cords
facts.quote: 46% of holiday decorators admit to daisy-chaining power strips or extension cords, which can cause an electrical fire

facts.claim: 62% of Americans will decorate with lights, trees, wreaths or menorahs
facts.quote: A majority (62%) of Americans will decorate their homes with lights, trees, wreaths, menorahs, or all of the above this holiday season.

facts.claim: Other findings: 59% check for certification; 85% inspect lights and 87% inspect cords; 83% use weatherproof outlets outdoors
facts.quote: 59% of holiday decorators check to see if lighted decorations are tested and certified by an accredited organization ... 85% of holiday decorators inspect lights for damage and another 87% inspect power cords ... 83% of holiday decorators make sure outdoor lighted decorations are plugged into weatherproof outlets

facts.claim: Survey method: n=2,008 US adults, online, BV Insights, August 25 - September 1, 2026, margin +/- 2.2%
facts.quote: This nationally representative survey of n=2,008 U.S. adults was designed by ULSE and conducted online by BV Insights between August 25-September 1, 2026. The margin of sampling error for the survey at 95% confidence for aggregate results is +/- 2.2%.

facts.claim: UL: power strips (relocatable power taps, category XBYS) are intended to plug directly into a permanently installed receptacle and are not intended to be daisy chained to other strips or extension cords, nor used as a substitute for fixed wiring or routed through walls
facts.quote: Relocatable power taps are intended to be directly connected to a permanently installed branch circuit receptacle. Relocatable power taps are not intended to be series connected (daisy chained) to other relocatable power taps or to extension cords. ... nor are they intended to be used as a substitute for fixed wiring. The cords of relocatable power taps are not intended to be routed through walls, windows, ceilings, floors or other similar openings.
facts.method: browser (UL's answer in IAEI Magazine, March/April 2002, quoting its XBYS guide information)

facts.claim: NEC Article 590 permits decorative holiday lighting strings for up to 90 days; UL certifies them to UL 588; year-round 'string lights' are covered by UL 588 Supplement SD, added Sept. 15, 2017
facts.quote: Article 590 of the National Electrical Code® (NFPA 70®, 2023; NEC®) permits decorative holiday lighting strings to be used for up to 90 days. ... The basic standard used to investigate products in this category is UL 588, the Standard for Seasonal and Holiday Decorative Products. Requirements for string lights for all-year use are found in Supplement SD of UL 588. ... Supplement SD was added to UL 588 on Sept. 15, 2017

facts.claim: The load fitting marking on UL 588 year-round string lights states the string's watts and the maximum total watts connected end to end; 120 V maximum input
facts.quote: The load fitting marking is “CAUTION: This string light is rated ___Watts; do not overload. Connect other string lights end-to-end up to a maximum of ___ Watts total.” ... with a maximum input voltage rating of 120 V.

facts.claim: Residential branch circuits: a 15-amp circuit has 14 AWG copper conductors and a 15-amp maximum load; a 20-amp circuit 12 AWG and 20 amps
facts.quote: TABLE E3702.14 (Table 210.24) BRANCH-CIRCUIT REQUIREMENTS—SUMMARY ... CIRCUIT RATING 15 amp 20 amp 30 amp Conductors: Minimum size (AWG) circuit conductors 14 12 10 ... Maximum load (amperes) 15 20 30

facts.claim: Our arithmetic: a 15-amp circuit at 120 volts carries at most 1,800 watts; a 20-amp circuit 2,400 watts
facts.quote: 15 A x 120 V = 1,800 W; 20 A x 120 V = 2,400 W (calculation from g7 and g8)

facts.claim: NFPA: 835 home structure fires a year began with decorations (excluding trees), with 3 deaths, 29 injuries and $18 million damage; electrical distribution or lighting equipment was involved in 40% of home Christmas tree fires
facts.quote: U.S. fire departments responded to an estimated average of 835 home structure fires per year that began with decorations, excluding Christmas trees. These fires caused an annual average of 3 civilian fire deaths, 29 civilian fire injuries and $18 million in direct property damage. Electrical distribution or lighting equipment was involved in two in five (40%) home Christmas tree fires.

facts.claim: NFPA: 143 home Christmas tree fires a year in 2020-2024
facts.quote: Between 2020-2024, US fire departments responded to an average of 143 home fires that started with Christmas trees per year.

cut.claim: A 210-watt end-to-end limit for incandescent sets
cut.why: only retailer blogs; UL 588 text not opened
